newsitem.title: USA: Copley enters into plea agreement.
newsitem.headline: Copley enters into plea agreement.

text.p: Copley Pharmaceutical Inc said Monday directors voted to enter into a plea agreement covering all issues investigated by the Massachusetts U.S. Attorney, who is recommending a $10,650,000 fine.
The company also said it entered into an agreement with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration providing for an independent audit of 20 of Copley's approved Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
Copley said it will take an after tax charge of $2 million, or $0.10 per share, in the second quarter to revise its reserve for product-recall and litigation expenses.

The plea agreement covers criminal violations arising out of a nearly three-year-long review of changes Copley made prior to July 1994 in the manufacturing processes of four drugs regulated by the FDA, the company said.
A federal judge in Boston will be asked to accept the plea, the company added.

Copley said it is cooperating with the FDA, which has agreed it will continue to review Copley's pending applications that during the audit. The FDA will also accept new applications from the company, and, where appropriate, approve Copley applications during the review, it added.

This is the first corporate fine in a food and drug case imposed under new, stricter federal sentencing guidelines that call for higher penalties than prevailed in the past, Copley said, adding: "We are very disappointed, however, by the size of the fine. The principal point on which we and the U.S. Attorney agree is the desirability of resolving this investigation." ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
